sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Dynamic Redundancy and Budget Optimization Studio. Drag the corpus size, unit wage, and Tier 1 clear rate sliders to compare static triplication at m equals 3 against dynamic m equals 2 to 5 triage. Try clicking the Clinical Radiology 200k preset to see how an 85-10-5 distribution unlocks 225,000 dollars in net savings while increasing coverage on high-risk scans.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Check out that stacked labor allocation bar, Dr. Nova! By letting unanimous Tier 1 scans stop at m equals 2 instead of forcing 3 votes everywhere, we slash total labeling fees by over 23 percent and reinvest 5-expert oversight strictly into hard Tier 3 boundary disputes!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: On a corpus of 200,000 medical radiography scans costing 1 dollar 50 per vote, 85 percent resolve unanimously at m equals 2, 10 percent escalate to m equals 3, and 5 percent go to a 5-specialist panel. Compute the exact dollar and percentage savings versus uniform static triplication.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! Uniform triplication across 200,000 radiology scans requires 600,000 votes at 1 dollar 50, totaling 900,000 dollars. Tally the dynamic Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 annotations carefully and compute the net savings!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on, Protocol Architect! Uniform triplication requires 600,000 annotations costing 900,000 dollars. Dynamic triage consumes 340,000 Tier 1 votes, 60,000 Tier 2 votes, and 50,000 Tier 3 votes—totaling 450,000 annotations at 675,000 dollars. You save exactly 225,000 dollars, a 25 percent reduction, while deploying 5 specialists onto critical scans!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Compute each tier carefully: 85 percent times 200,000 times 2 gives 340,000 votes; 10 percent times 200,000 times 3 adds 60,000; and 5 percent times 200,000 times 5 adds 50,000—totaling 450,000 annotations at 675,000 dollars versus 900,000 static, saving exactly 225,000 dollars or 25 percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Bayesian Elo Worker Auditor and Golden Honeypot Simulator. Choose a task difficulty between 1,200 and 1,800 and click Inject Golden Honeypot Batch or Simulate Bot Slip. Watch the live Audit Event Stream compute expected probabilities E-sub-w and automatically trigger QUARANTINED badges whenever ratings cross below 1,200.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Watch how fast that works, Dr. Nova! When you inject easy 1,200 honeypots or force a bot failure, failing high-expectation checks crushes sloppy workers right beneath the 1,200 quarantine wall while verified doctors climb steadily above 1,800!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: A medical pipeline produces 4,200 daily disagreements far exceeding a 3-doctor panel's 300-item daily limit, while skilled new radiologists stall at default prior ratings under a low constant K-factor. Which paired engineering architecture resolves both bottlenecks?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2! How do you compress 4,200 messy splits into 300 high-value clinical reviews without exhausting your MDs—and fix newcomer Elo cold-start delays at the exact same time? Pick Option A, B, or C!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely right! Multiplying disagreement by gradient loss norm and liability weight W-sub-class concentrates the 300 doctor slots strictly onto high-impact clinical risks, while crowd committees and auto-averaging clear routine noise. Meanwhile, inverse-square-root tenure decay starts K-sub-w high at 48 for fast newcomer promotion and stabilizes veterans at the 12 floor!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Careful! Randomly sampling the 4,200 disputes drops high-liability cancers, and a low constant K-factor traps qualified new doctors in rookie queues for dozens of batches. True governance combines gradient-and-liability Priority routing to cap MD queues at 300 with tenure-discounted K-sub-w decaying from 48 to 12.
